overview:
Need a quick reset from Delhi without burning your leave? This **1 Night / 2 Days** weekend getaway takes you into the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, where two very different kinds of calm sit roughly 50-60 km apart. It's a lovely fit whether you're travelling for faith, for the mountains, or for both.

Mukteshwar is famous for its 350-year-old Shiva temple and wide, panoramic views of the Himalayas. Kainchi Dham is home to the ashram of Neem Karoli Baba, a place people visit for its deep sense of peace. Day 1 is all about arriving in Mukteshwar and settling in, and Day 2 is for adventure and sightseeing, with stops at Kainchi Dham, Mukteshwar Temple, Chowli ki Jaali, Balugarh Waterfall and Nainital or Bhimtal.

We handle the round-trip transfers from Delhi, one night in Swiss camps or rooms, a breakfast, a dinner and an evening high tea. When the sun goes down, there's a bonfire and music evening, and an enthusiastic, experienced trip captain keeps everything running smoothly so you can just sit back and enjoy the hills.

faqs.a: It's a 1 Night / 2 Days weekend getaway with one night of stay in Swiss camps or rooms.

Round-trip transfers from Delhi, one night's accommodation in Swiss camps or rooms, one breakfast, one dinner and an evening high tea, sightseeing as per the itinerary, a bonfire and music evening, and an experienced trip captain.

overview:
Beaches, islands, a full moon party and a whole lot of sea spray: this **6 Nights / 7 Days** Thailand group trip packs the best of the south into one week. You arrive in Phuket, Thailand's largest island, nestled in the Andaman Sea, and head straight to Krabi for a 4 Island tour by speedboat.

From there it's over to Koh Samui to explore the island, a trip across to Koh Phangan for the famous full moon party, and a leisure day to just slow down. Then you're back in Phuket for a city walk and pub crawl, followed by a speedboat day trip to Phi Phi Island, the place that shared the screen with Leonardo DiCaprio in The Beach. Think limestone karsts rising out of the sea, lush green cover and waves breaking over coral reefs. Phuket's Sino-colonial buildings, Big Buddha and Wat Chalong give you a glimpse of its eclectic culture too.

We take care of airport pick-up and drop at the destination city, 6 nights of accommodation, 6 breakfasts and 2 lunches (on the Phi Phi and Krabi island tours), plus all the ferries, speedboats and transfers between Krabi, Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Phuket. 5% GST and 5% TCS are already included.

faqs.q: How long is the Thailand trip?
faqs.a: It's a 6 Nights / 7 Days trip covering Phuket, Krabi, Koh Samui and Koh Phangan, with 6 nights of accommodation.

Airport pick-up and drop at the destination city, 6 nights' accommodation, 6 breakfasts and 2 lunches, the Phi Phi day trip and Krabi Four Island tour by speedboat, the Koh Samui to Phuket bus and ferry transfer, Koh Samui to Koh Phangan and back by speedboat, ferry and transfers from Koh Samui to Krabi, and 5% GST and 5% TCS.

The visa is not included. For flights, check the Inclusions & Exclusions section or ask our team.

overview:
Royal palaces, shimmering lakes and one of Rajasthan's mightiest forts: this **2 Nights / 3 Days** weekend getaway is a proper slice of Mewar history set in the Aravalli hills. Udaipur brings the romance, with its lakes and palaces, while Kumbhalgarh brings the grandeur, with its formidable fort that is part of a UNESCO World Heritage listing.

Day 1 you reach Udaipur and kick off with a city tour. Day 2 is for Udaipur sightseeing, including the City Palace, one of the largest palace complexes in Rajasthan on the banks of Lake Pichola, and a boat ride on the lake (sunset is the time to go) for views of the City Palace and the Lake Palace on its island. Day 3 you head out to Kumbhalgarh Fort before the journey back.

We cover all transportation and sightseeing to and from Gurugram in an A/C vehicle, 2 nights in a hotel in Udaipur, 4 meals (2 breakfasts and 2 dinners), and a tour curator who keeps the weekend easy and fun.

overview:
From buzzing city nights to misty limestone bays, this **7 Nights / 8 Days** Vietnam group trip runs the length of the country. Vietnam stretches along the eastern coast of the Indochina Peninsula, bordering China, Laos and Cambodia, with a long coastline on the South China Sea, and its mix of history, culture and landscapes is hard to beat.

You start in Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon), the economic hub of French colonial landmarks and modern skyscrapers, with a city stroll and nightlife. Next comes a full-day Cu Chi Tunnels tour with the War Remnants Museum. Then it's Da Nang for beach time and the Dragon Bridge, a Ba Na Hills day with the cable car, Golden Hand Bridge and French Village, and a bamboo basket boat ride plus a Hoi An Ancient Town tour with a lantern boat ride.

The north brings Hanoi, the capital known for its centuries-old architecture, lakes and street food, where you explore the Old Quarter, catch the buzz of Train Street and party on Beer Street. The grand finale is a Ha Long Bay cruise with kayaking, cave exploration and an overnight stay among the emerald waters and limestone cliffs, before departure day.

faqs.q: How long is the Vietnam trip?
faqs.a: It's a 7 Nights / 8 Days trip covering Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hoi An, Hanoi and Ha Long Bay.

Ho Chi Minh City, a full-day Cu Chi Tunnels tour with the War Remnants Museum, Da Nang's beach and Dragon Bridge, Ba Na Hills, a bamboo basket boat ride and Hoi An Ancient Town, Hanoi's Old Quarter and Train Street, and a Ha Long Bay cruise with kayaking and cave exploration.

overview:
In winter, Spiti Valley turns this high-altitude cold desert in Himachal Pradesh into a silent, snow-covered wonderland. Temperatures can plunge to -20°C or lower, rivers freeze, ancient monasteries like Key and Tabo sit under snow, and it's the best season for a chance to spot the elusive snow leopard. This **6 Nights / 7 Days** backpacking trip is for travellers who want the real, raw winter experience.

With the Manali route closed in winter, you travel via Shimla through Kinnaur. The journey starts with an AC bus from Delhi to Shimla, then heads to Sangla and Chitkul, on through Khab to Nako, across Chicham Bridge to Key Monastery, up to Hikkim, Komic and Langza, and back via Kaza to Kalpa before the return from Shimla to Delhi. Expect frozen waterfalls, snowy monasteries and serious stargazing.

We cover the AC bus between Delhi and Shimla, all sightseeing by tempo traveller, 6 nights of stay, 12 meals, all inner line permits, a team captain throughout, an oxygen cylinder in the tempo traveller, and driver charges, tolls, parking and fuel. Most hotels shut in the cold, so stays are mostly village homestays with basic, hearty local food and limited water. Pack warm and come with an adventurous spirit.

faqs.q: How long is the Winter Spiti trip?
faqs.a: It's a 6 Nights / 7 Days backpacking trip, with 6 nights of accommodation.
The trip starts with an AC bus transfer from Delhi to Shimla and ends with the transfer from Shimla back to Delhi. Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

AC bus transfers from Delhi to Shimla and back, all sightseeing by tempo traveller, 6 nights of accommodation, 12 meals, all inner line permits, a team captain throughout, an oxygen cylinder 24/7 in the tempo traveller, and driver night charges, tolls, parking and fuel.

5% GST, extra food and drinks, sightseeing or activity tickets, travel insurance, medical expenses beyond first aid, tips, laundry, mineral water and personal items, and any extra cost from landslides, road closures or other unforeseen events.
The trip starts from ₹16,999 per person on Quad Sharing. Triple Sharing is ₹17,999 and Dual Sharing is ₹18,999 per person, with 5% GST extra.

faqs.q: How cold does it get and what are the stays like?
faqs.a: Temperatures can drop to -20°C or lower. Most hotels close in winter, so village homestays are the main option, with limited water, often no running water in bathrooms, and basic local food.

faqs.q: Why does the route go via Shimla and not Manali?
faqs.a: The Manali route is closed in winter, so the journey goes via Shimla through Kinnaur.
